name: Ricardian socialism
summary: Ricardian socialism was a British current of the 1820s to 1840s that turned the labour theory of value against capitalists and landlords, holding that workers are entitled to the whole produce of their labour and that rent, profit and interest are unearned deductions from it. Its remedies were peaceful and varied: Thompson's cooperative communities, Gray's national bank and labour money, Bray's equal exchange through producers' companies, and Hodgskin's free-market individualism. It rejected Malthus and held that low wages cause gluts.
scope: The mainstream of the school as documented by William Thompson, John Gray, Thomas Hodgskin and John Francis Bray (1824-1839), with Hall, Ravenstone and Edmonds only as background. Hodgskin's near-anarchist individualism is a minority strand, so most state-role answers are medium or low and neutral where the four split. Most modern issues were never addressed and are low confidence.

keyFigures.name: William Thompson
keyFigures.role: Irish author of An Inquiry into the Principles of the Distribution of Wealth (1824), the first systematic statement of the school's exploitation theory

keyFigures.name: Thomas Hodgskin
keyFigures.role: Author of Labour Defended against the Claims of Capital (1825), the school's best-known critic of capital's claims

keyFigures.name: John Francis Bray
keyFigures.role: Author of Labour's Wrongs and Labour's Remedy (1839), proposing equal exchange through producers' joint-stock companies

universal-healthcare.rationale: Never discussed; a movement claiming the whole produce for workers and relief of poverty would likely favour guaranteed care, but their remedies were cooperative exchange, not state services.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage floors do not appear in their writings; Hodgskin saw wages settling by free bargaining while Bray wanted uniform pay for equal hours, so adherents split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: They attacked competition as an engine of mischief (Gray) and unequal exchange (Bray), though Hodgskin trusted free markets once monopolies ended, so the mainstream leans against.

public-ownership.rationale: Gray's national bank and warehouses and Bray's national joint-stock scheme imply collective ownership, but Hodgskin was hostile to government and Thompson favoured self-governing communities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from their view that rent, profit and interest are unearned incomes; no tax programme is documented, and the preferred remedy was exchange reform and cooperation.

unions-good.rationale: Hodgskin defended workers' combinations as no crime and as giving labourers moral strength through common interest; Thompson and Bray backed workers' self-organisation.

property-fundamental.rationale: Bray held private property to be the root of poverty and unfair dealing, and Hodgskin argued property rights rested on slavery rather than justice, though both accepted the producer's right to their own product.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Joint-stock companies were a tool in Bray's scheme and Hodgskin opposed state intervention; the issue of regulating corporations was not addressed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not discussed; their concern was that workers be paid the whole produce, and they would see poverty as made by institutions, so cutting relief would not be favoured.

worker-ownership.rationale: Thompson's cooperative communities with eventual worker ownership of land and capital and Bray's allied joint-stock companies of producers put the means of production in producers' hands.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anachronistic; Hodgskin's hostility to state power and the radical-reform tradition suggests distrust of surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed by any of them; nothing in the labour-value critique points either way.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the radical press-and-expression liberties of the 1820s-40s and Hodgskin's distrust of legislators.

strong-leader.rationale: Hodgskin attacked governors as self-willed men and Bray worked within Chartist democratic politics; rule by one person to bypass gridlock runs against their popular-reform outlook.

state-harmful.rationale: Hodgskin verged on anarchism and called government a set of self-willed men, but Gray and Bray used national banks and state-issued currency, so the school was split.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no basis for a side.

empower-police-military.rationale: Hodgskin said the legislature of capitalists and landlords keeps labourers in subjection through law; more coercive force would be seen as serving them.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Thompson championed women's rights but sex work is not discussed; inferred split between liberty and concern about economic coercion.

decide-locally.rationale: Thompson favoured small self-reliant communities and Hodgskin distrusted central legislatures; Gray's national bank pulls the other way.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from Thompson's utilitarian reform outlook and the belief that circumstances and institutions, not nature, produce social ills.

traditional-family.rationale: Thompson argued in his Appeal for women's equality and saw cooperation as securing equality of the sexes, so traditional hierarchical family roles were not endorsed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic and undiscussed; Thompson's radical utilitarianism may suggest openness but nothing documents it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not discussed; Thompson backed contraception as a response to poverty, but abortion is not documented.

more-religion-public.rationale: Thompson was an atheist and Hodgskin mocked the priest and idol-worship of capital; a larger public religious role is not a goal.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; their critique concerned class, so no specific position on racial remedies can be sourced.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Thompson's Appeal argued that women's subordination was produced by law and custom rather than nature, though he did not use this language.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: They were not concerned with national culture; the question is outside their writings.

gradual-change.rationale: They shared the Utopian faith in peaceful change; Bray envisaged producers gradually buying out owners, though they sought deep economic transformation, not preserving institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not discussed; no basis in sources for a side.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed; no international institutions existed in their time and they did not theorise them.

free-trade.rationale: Hodgskin advocated free trade in the enlarged sense and Thompson was a liberal economist; Gray favoured protecting labour, but the mainstream was not protectionist.

nation-first.rationale: Not addressed; their concern was class and exchange, not national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed in their works; no sourced position.

limit-growth.rationale: They saw production as limited by bad distribution and money (Gray) and wanted abundance for workers, so limiting growth runs against their outlook.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in their writings.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Hodgskin said machines are inert without skilled labour and the Ricardians held that the gains of machinery go to capital, so progress depends on who owns it.

revolution-justified.rationale: They shared the Utopian faith in peaceful change; Bray proposed a peaceful transition and Thompson relied on voluntary communities, though the movement did not rule out Chartist agitation.

experts-over-public.rationale: Bray and Thompson put faith in popular and democratic bodies such as elected boards of trade; Hodgskin distrusted officials, so expert rule is not favoured.

central-planning.rationale: Their schemes were exchange systems, labour money and cooperative communities with market-like exchange of equal labour; Gray's national warehouses are the closest but not a plan.

socialized-markets.rationale: Bray's equal exchange between producer companies and Gray's labour money kept exchange while removing private profit, close to this view.

land-value-tax.rationale: Rent was viewed as unearned income, but they offered no single-tax proposal; Hodgskin extended rent critique to capital as well.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Bray wanted inherited wealth used for the benefit of all, pointing toward heavy inheritance taxation or transfer.

basic-income.rationale: Hodgskin and the school insisted that income should flow from labour; an unconditional income conflicts with this principle.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Hodgskin backed free trade; Gray's views on tariffs are not documented, so the answer is an inference.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Gray's national bank issuing labour-based currency would steer production, but Hodgskin opposed state intervention; split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Hodgskin and Thompson accepted the producer's property in their product but Bray and Thompson moved to common ownership; the school leaned toward producer ownership rather than corporations or state.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Gray and Bray reformed money into labour-time notes and kept equal wages for equal hours, not abolishing them; Thompson's communities were more communal.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Gray proposed a national bank issuing paper currency based on labour time, the opposite of leaving money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Bray's boards of trade were elected, not state-recognised corporate bodies setting prices with employers; not a documented goal.

one-party-rule.rationale: Bray was a Chartist working in democratic politics and the school was reformist and pre-Leninist; single-party rule is foreign to it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Radicals in Hodgskin's circle attacked a ruling class of landlords and capitalists; no monarchical stance is documented.

democracy-best.rationale: Thompson defended women's suffrage against Mill's male-only case and Bray was a Chartist, so democratic rights were supported though economic reform was seen as prior.

direct-votes.rationale: Bray's elected boards of trade and Chartism imply democratic enthusiasm, but direct legislation by plebiscite is not documented.

workers-councils.rationale: Anachronistic; Bray's elected boards of trade are the nearest parallel but he did not make them the basis of political power.

right-to-secede.rationale: The school wrote about class and exchange, not about territorial questions, so adherents have no documented view on secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Hodgskin opposed rule by the self-willed few and the school held that ruling classes arise from property history, not natural fitness.

political-violence-never.rationale: They preferred peaceful remedies but did not formulate an absolute rule; Hall and Hodgskin used strong language yet urged no violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Thompson's utilitarian, cooperative outlook cannot be squared with glorifying war; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Thompson was an atheist and Hodgskin criticised the priesthood; inferred support for separation from their anticlerical radicalism.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Thompson was an atheist and grounded ethics in utilitarian happiness; Hodgskin appealed to natural law, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Hodgskin verged on anarchism but did not advance private defence; the broader school relied on public institutions.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; peace and cooperation themes imply low priority on military rivalry.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Thompson's universalist utilitarianism and championing of the equality of the sexes implies a universalist outlook; not discussed.

class-struggle-history.rationale: They contrasted classes of producers and idlers and Thompson and Edmonds saw stages of history, but their faith in peaceful reform differed from the later Marxist view of class conflict as the driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Thompson argued from utilitarianism for equal distribution with preserved incentives, while Gray and Bray proposed equal exchange and uniform pay for equal hours.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Their sources discuss landlords' rent, not indigenous peoples, so no position on indigenous authority is documented.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Colonial debts between nations are absent from their writings, which dealt with domestic distribution of wealth.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; their universalist concerns suggest scepticism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Thompson's utilitarianism valued security and incentive, but they criticised competitive acquisitiveness in favour of cooperation; split. The cited sources do not address this directly, so the answer is inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Thompson's utilitarian and rights-based case for women suggests rights-first; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The school treated nature as a source of wealth alongside labour and never discussed its value in itself.

limit-population.rationale: They unanimously rejected Malthus's population theory as the cause of poverty, yet Thompson supported contraception, so population control is not central.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: They wanted to reform distribution of industry's wealth, not abandon it; Hodgskin and others praised productive power, with the evil lying in appropriation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed beyond views on who gains from machinery.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement lies centuries beyond their concerns; nothing in their principles points either way.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from their trust in popular institutions.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy is anachronistic for 1820s to 1840s radicals, so no position can be derived from their sources.

restore-past-order.rationale: They looked forward to cooperation and equal exchange, although Hall and Ravenstone had some nostalgia for earlier arrangements.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Thompson's utilitarianism judged institutions by their results for happiness, but the school also held fixed natural-right claims.

direct-action.rationale: Hodgskin defended combinations but the school sought peaceful reform, exchange schemes and communities rather than direct action against parliaments.

means-match-ends.rationale: Thompson and Owenites sought to build cooperative communities by voluntary means that embody the society wanted; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: They wanted abundance fairly shared through industry and trade; nothing in the school favours primitive life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hodgskin treated division of labour and interdependence as the basis of production ("so dependent is man on man"), not something to abolish.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Their principle was reward proportional to labour performed (the whole produce to the labourer), not need.

production-for-use.rationale: Underconsumptionist views and Gray's warehouse system aimed at production meeting wants, but they kept exchange value measured by labour.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Core doctrine: rent, profit and interest are unearned incomes taken from labour, termed surplus value by Thompson and described by Bray as unequal exchange.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Pre-Marxist and peaceful in outlook; Bray favoured peaceful purchase of capital, not rule over former classes.

collective-farming.rationale: Thompson's village communities held land in common, but Gray and Hodgskin did not propose it.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; their underconsumption theory dealt with gluts, not imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Hodgskin was hostile to rulers and thought profit legalised robbery, but he did not call taxation theft; the school generally saw tax as less harmful than rent and profit.

harm-principle.rationale: Hodgskin's natural liberty leaned this way, but the school did not take a stated stance.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Hodgskin was individualist; Thompson and Bray favoured community ownership; split.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from Hodgskin's distrust of coercive state power and the radical outlook.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Bray and Thompson emphasised democratic political voice and rights; not addressed directly.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from their critique of commercial competition.

positive-liberty.rationale: Bray held that political equality is empty without economic equality, and Thompson wanted security for the labourer, linking freedom to material conditions.

media-academia-power.rationale: They criticised legislators as landlords and capitalists, not universities or media, so this claim is outside their analysis.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Thompson's environmentalist utilitarianism and championing of equality rules out innate hierarchy; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Bray's elected boards of trade resemble trade bodies, but he sought democratic representation; not a stated principle.

total-state.rationale: Hodgskin was hostile to government and no member advocated a state directing all of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; reformist, cooperative outlook is opposed.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Inferred from Thompson's utilitarianism and the cooperative-peace outlook of the school.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The school attacked landlord and capitalist rule and favoured equal rights; feudal lordship is the opposite of their outlook.

bound-labor.rationale: Hodgskin said property rested on slavery rather than justice and the school demanded labour's freedom and its whole produce, so bound labour is the type of arrangement they condemned.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Anachronistic; Hodgskin did say property law serves ruling interests, but no epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: Thompson's utilitarianism and Hodgskin's natural-law appeals assume universal standards knowable by reason.

single-common-good.rationale: Thompson's greatest-happiness principle aims at one good worked out by reason, but they also stressed class interests of producers and idlers.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Nationhood and Zionism arose after the school and its sources never touch the subject.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora and homeland rights are not addressed in their sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language policy is absent from their economic writings.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Thompson's cooperative communities and Bray's boards and companies of producers imply democratic control by workers over enterprises.

school-vouchers.rationale: Thompson favoured education as a community good but vouchers were not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: They held that underconsumption caused gluts and rejected Say's law, so they would favour demand-supporting measures, though deficit spending was not discussed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Hodgskin held something like this view, but Gray and Bray proposed state-run banking and exchange, and Bray held political rights as depending on economic equality.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; Hodgskin criticised rulers and relied on law and natural right.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed; Thompson supported Irish reform but no doctrine documented.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Thompson was an atheist rationalist who tried to unite political economy with utilitarian morality, and Hodgskin used rationalist deist argument.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility by citizenship was not discussed; their remedy was producers' ownership of the produce, not benefits.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The school held that those who labour should enjoy the produce and condemned idle capitalists, but did not discuss welfare conditions.

class-collaboration.rationale: They distinguished producers from idle capitalists and landlords whose claims were unjust; Thompson contrasted competition with cooperation among producers, not between classes.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; reformist outlook is opposed.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western fronts belong to a much later anticolonial era and have no counterpart in their sources.

workers-nation.rationale: The school did not debate whether the working class should organise nationally or internationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Thompson's Appeal argued for equal rights between the sexes, rebutting Mill's case for male-only suffrage.

ban-interest.rationale: Hodgskin treated interest as legalised robbery, and Gray and Bray attacked interest and the money system, though their remedy was reform of exchange rather than an outright ban.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Inferred from Thompson's equal-worth utilitarianism; no direct statement.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Hodgskin said the legislature of capitalists and landlords makes laws that keep labourers subject, and Bray said political inequality follows economic inequality.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Fossil fuel policy is anachronistic; the sources contain no energy policy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration and assimilation are not discussed in the sources used for this audit.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy of this kind is absent from their thought; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems were not their concern; Chartism, which Bray joined, asked for the vote and equal districts instead.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from cooperative and peaceful outlook.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Thompson held that law and custom subordinate women and wrote his Appeal against it; the language is later.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Hodgskin described governors as a sordid set of self-willed men and claimed laws serve landlords and capitalists.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from Thompson's egalitarian ethics; not discussed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional justice and accountability for security forces were not subjects the school wrote on.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Hodgskin came close, but the broader school (Gray's bank, Bray's national exchange, Thompson's reform) wanted more than defence of property, which they saw as unjust.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred from Thompson's universalism; no direct statement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Thompson's utilitarianism counts everyone's happiness equally and his Appeal demanded equal rights for women.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Anachronistic; they advanced local communities and national schemes that could be built peacefully without foreign revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism is outside the documented concerns of the school.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal laws were not a subject of their writing.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from rationalist, freethinking Thompson and Hodgskin.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Thompson was a vegetarian but did not advocate banning; not a school position.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from Thompson's atheism and rationalism.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a later Soviet-era doctrine with no counterpart in a pre-Marxian reformist school.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Bray's Chartist democracy and Thompson's defence of equal suffrage rest on popular consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Hodgskin's free-trade stance and the classical political economy they used reject the mercantilist aim.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Hodgskin's individualism leans that way, but the rest accept state action; not a stated rule.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Gray called competition a tremendous engine of mischief and Thompson contrasted competitive with cooperative systems, arguing progress is cooperative.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred from the radical democratic tradition of Chartism.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Hodgskin's claim that labourers are held in subjection by laws serving capitalists matches the idea of domination, though the term is modern.

separated-powers.rationale: Hodgskin criticised the legislature's class bias, but no school position on separating powers is documented.

vanguard-party.rationale: Pre-Leninist; Bray and the school relied on popular education, exchange schemes and peaceful reform.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Thompson's utilitarian case for more equal distribution and the school's focus on the producing poor favour giving priority to labourers.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing did not exist; nothing in their principles speaks to tenant purchase rights.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Hodgskin wrote that combination is of itself no crime and defended workers' unions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: They unanimously rejected Malthusian population theory and attributed poverty to institutions that take rent, profit and interest from labour.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition was not discussed; they favoured elected boards in Bray's scheme, but not as a doctrine on lotteries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from Hodgskin and the radical suspicion of governors.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; Hodgskin opposed intervention but Gray and Bray set prices by labour cost.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred from radical press freedom and Hodgskin's hostility to government.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred; Bray's Chartism and the school's non-statist reform imply no party army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not discussed in the sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Chartism, which Bray joined, demanded payment of MPs to open office to workers, but this exact standard is not documented.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline is a later question; no position on bound party members is documented.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational unions were not conceivable in their time and the sources are silent.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred from atheist Thompson and anticlerical Hodgskin.

clerical-rule.rationale: Thompson was an atheist and Hodgskin ridiculed priests; theocracy is opposed.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a twentieth-century doctrine with no equivalent in this pre-Marxian school.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from radical freedom of the press.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term rules are outside the sources; Chartist annual parliaments hint at short terms but not for presidents.

recall-officials.rationale: Chartism's annual parliaments suggest openness to this, but not documented for the school.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not addressed in the sources.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Hodgskin held rent was a surplus from land and did not keep labourers poor, and no one proposed banning rental.

people-in-arms.rationale: The school did not discuss militias or armed citizenry in the sources used here.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Thompson's village communities involved rural settings, but they praised industry; split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not addressed in the sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Thompson prized education and reason; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from Thompson's utilitarian reformism and Hodgskin's later writing against the criminal system.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Thompson backed contraception and women's equality; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Thompson was an atheist rationalist and Hodgskin a deist.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Obscenity law is not discussed; their sources focus on exchange and property.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not discussed in the sources.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language rights are not part of the documented positions.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general laws on religious grounds are not discussed in the sources.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; Thompson's lifestyle reforms were personal choices.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt of poor countries is anachronistic for this school; no position is documented.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Bray argued that political equality follows economic equality, a parallel for this claim, though independence is anachronistic here.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; Chartism's Charter was legislative, not an assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from radical liberty and anti-authoritarian outlook.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is anachronistic and absent from their writings, which dealt with domestic distribution.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons did not exist and defence doctrine is not discussed.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidential election mode is not addressed in the sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Gray proposed a national bank issuing labour-based currency, so he would not favour stable-price independence as primary aim; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Peace settlements over land claims are not discussed in the sources.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Bray held that property built unequal exchange and wanted inherited wealth used for all, and Thompson judged distribution by happiness.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet Union post-dates the school entirely, so no view is documented.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is anachronistic for this school.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance doctrines like collective defence are not in the sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Anticlerical outlooks suggest sympathy, but no policy documented.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a ceremonial head of state is not addressed in the sources.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Military suppression of secession is not addressed in the sources.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special autonomy arrangements within a larger state are not discussed in the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Atheist Thompson and deist, anti-authority Hodgskin would reject sacral monarchy.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from their redistributive concern; not discussed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Thompson, following Owen, held that circumstances form character, so poverty and vice are produced by institutions.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Hodgskin criticised rulers acting for their own interest and the school demanded laws grounded in justice.

space-expansion.rationale: Spaceflight lies beyond their world, so no position can be derived.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not a documented concern of the school.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not discussed, though Thompson argued for sexual equality in general.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Anachronistic; they expected cooperation to end class division.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rent was viewed as an unearned income, but Hodgskin argued the landlord's share does not keep labourers poor and no common programme of confiscation existed.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not discussed in the sources.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Thompson was an atheist and free-thinker.

common-currency.rationale: Gray proposed a national labour-based currency, but shared multinational currencies are not discussed.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions are not addressed in the sources.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural autonomy is not discussed in the sources.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority emigration versus equal rights is not discussed in the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Thompson and Edmonds outlined stages of economic history and Hodgskin treated capitalist laws as historical, but they also stressed moral argument.

ban-cartels.rationale: Hodgskin wanted an end to state-enforced monopolies; others not documented.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts of failing firms are not discussed; they held that gluts come from low wages, not bad management.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The balance between courts and majorities is not discussed in the sources.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Thompson wanted women's equal rights, but quotas are anachronistic.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreements with standards clauses are anachronistic; Hodgskin favoured free trade, but nothing on standards is documented.

moral-incentives.rationale: Thompson held that equal distribution was best when incentives to produce were preserved; the school held reward by labour performed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Bray wanted inherited wealth used for all and the school attacked rank resting on landlord and capitalist claims.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Curriculum choices about national history are not discussed in the sources.

patriotic-education.rationale: Patriotic schooling is not addressed in the sources.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is anachronistic and not discussed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Gray's national bank issuing paper currency based on labour time and Bray's state-issued paper currency are public money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: They rejected Say's law, argued low wages limit demand causing gluts, and saw capitalism as transient.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence is not discussed in the sources.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Anachronistic; they treated workers as uniformly exploited.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Thompson's equal-rights stance.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Entrenched constitutional rights are not discussed in the sources.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial-era boundary treaties are not discussed in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Bray's Chartist politics and Thompson's reform advocacy favour elected rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Not addressed; their communities were voluntary but ruled by agreement, so absolute veto not stated.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Hodgskin said rulers' laws serve their own interest but no right of resistance was stated.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Hodgskin criticised the legislature as a body of capitalists and landlords, though others sought reform of Parliament.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Thompson, a vegetarian for his last years, reflects Benthamite concern for sentient suffering.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Thompson was vegetarian but others not.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: They rejected charity from the idle rich and demanded labour's whole produce as a right, not a favour.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Bray was active in Chartism and Thompson campaigned for reform.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Cultural hegemony theory is a later development, absent from this school.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hodgskin spoke of prejudices distorting reward and capital as an idol, but this thesis is not developed.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; their exploitation analysis was national.

native-born-offices.rationale: Restricting offices to native-born citizens is not discussed in the sources.

party-own-road.rationale: Relations between national communist parties post-date the school.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Thompson favoured self-reliant communities but not international development.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist demands are not discussed in the sources.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous leadership claims are not discussed in the sources.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fascism post-dates the school, so no position is documented.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The fascism and communism comparison is anachronistic for this school.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The sources do not discuss the American Civil War.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument controversies are anachronistic and not in the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Contemporary gender-policy disputes are not in the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Contemporary gender-policy disputes are not in the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Civilisational variants of government are not discussed in the sources.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from radical hostility to coercive state forces.

paid-care-work.rationale: Thompson held that labour deserves its whole produce and wanted women's independence, but domestic wages are not documented.

filial-duty.rationale: Duties of grown children are not discussed in the sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service examinations are not discussed in the sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Thompson's Appeal criticised marriage law subordinating wives; inferred support for freer divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Chartism favoured annual parliaments and accountability, but delegation is not documented for Bray.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Thompson's communities held land in common, but individual tenure by use is not their formula.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary control of budgets is not discussed in the sources.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not discussed in the sources.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Restricting foreign land ownership is not documented in the sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine is anachronistic and not in the sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Their concern was distribution, not consumption of goods; underconsumptionists wanted more consumption by workers.

corporate-influence.rationale: Hodgskin said legislators are capitalists and landlords who make laws in their interest; the point extends to lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding of civil society is anachronistic and not in the sources.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Thompson backed contraception and the school was not pronatalist.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local residency rules for property purchase are not discussed in the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: Thompson's communities and Owenite work schemes gave work to all, but state guarantee not documented.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic peace theory is not discussed in the sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Hodgskin treated unjust laws as artificial but did not deny a duty to obey.

non-intervention.rationale: Interstate non-intervention is not discussed in the sources.

industrial-unions.rationale: The craft versus industrial union debate came later; Hodgskin only defended journeymen's combinations in general.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Thompson criticised marriage law for women, but abolishing it is not documented.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information rights are not discussed in the sources.

local-production.rationale: Thompson's self-sufficient communities favoured local production but others did not.

informal-organisation.rationale: Bray and Thompson organised through Chartism and cooperative congresses.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The relation of national to international law is not discussed in the sources.

religious-nation.rationale: Thompson was an atheist and the school had no religious definition of nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary systems between states are not discussed in the sources.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional fiscal retention is not discussed in the sources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Hodgskin and others upheld the producer's right to what labour produces, which includes personal goods.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anachronistic; Thompson's voluntary communism would regard such a view as hostile.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The mix of providers in public services is not discussed in the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: Thompson was an atheist and Hodgskin used religious language against capital as an idol, but no common theory of religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Thompson and Edmonds viewed capitalism as progressive but transient in a progression toward mutual cooperation.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Thompson argued cooperative association would secure equality between women and men.

socialized-care.rationale: Owenite communities shared child rearing, but Thompson's position is not documented here.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not discussed in the sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not discussed in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Thompson favoured small self-reliant communities with eventual worker ownership; Hodgskin and Gray did not, so the school only partly agrees.

majority-settlement.rationale: Majority settlement in minority regions is not discussed in the sources.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: They criticised capitalism but Thompson endorsed cooperative communism while Gray and Bray sought equal exchange; some see a middle course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical or religious land claims are not discussed in the sources.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Benthamite liberal utilitarianism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred from radicals' own persecution and demands for free expression and combination.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Atheist Thompson and deist Hodgskin were free-thinkers.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Islamic doctrine on jihad is outside the school's sources.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Thompson's self-governing communities and Bray's elected boards suggest broad participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Thompson linked women's subordination and labour exploitation but anachronistic framing.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Gender identity law is anachronistic and not in the sources.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is not discussed in the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Anachronistic; they presented themselves in a radical reform tradition.

alienated-labor.rationale: Hodgskin held that capital's power arises from the labourer's skill but is taken from him, and anticipated fetishism; close to alienation though not the term.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Atheist Thompson grounded authority in the happiness of the greatest number.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress in state institutions is not discussed in the sources.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace non-disclosure agreements are anachronistic and not in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Not addressed; their reforms differ from a mixed economy of this type.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The sources do not discuss abolishing armies.

rich-first.rationale: Thompson's egalitarian distribution and the school's equal exchange reject letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Great-power blocs post-date the school, so no position is documented.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary rule contradicts the school's attack on inherited privilege and elite rule.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Gray's national bank issuing currency on labour time and Bray's schemes remove usurious interest, resembling cost-price credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF-style conditionality is anachronistic and not in the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: Bray was active in Chartism, which demanded the vote for working men without property qualification.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist argument is later; Thompson's feminism did not link women to nature.

reification.rationale: Hodgskin anticipated Marx's fetishism by arguing economists wrongly credited capital with productive power.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Bray held political rights are empty without economic equality, though press ownership itself is not documented.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Hodgskin appealed to justice and natural rights against arbitrary legislation; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Thompson insisted on equal suffrage including women.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation is anachronistic and not in the sources.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data publication is anachronistic and not in the sources.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Randomly selected citizen bodies are not discussed in the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Thompson was an atheist, so reform of religious law was not his concern, and others did not address it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Bray held economic inequality produces political inequality, and Hodgskin held that legislators serve landlords and capitalists.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Military service by gay people is anachronistic and not in the sources.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Thompson was an atheist but favoured voluntary persuasion; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Hodgskin later wrote on the criminal system but proposed reform, not abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational power sharing is not discussed in the sources.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Their argument was that workers have a right to the produce of their labour, not charity; Hodgskin saw the poor as robbed, not as needing alms.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is anachronistic and not in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential risk concerns are anachronistic and not in the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Thompson's Appeal demanded equal rights for women.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Thompson's Appeal argued against male dominion in marriage and for equal rights.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voting rights for foreign residents are not discussed in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Hodgskin argued rent does not keep labourers poor and the school did not address housing.

abolish-ip.rationale: Hodgskin criticised monopolies enforced by the state, but patents and copyrights are not discussed in the sources.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is anachronistic and not in the sources.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign basing is not discussed in the sources.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Official genocide recognition is anachronistic and not in the sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Core doctrine: rent, profit and interest are unearned and labour is entitled to its whole produce.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: National continuity myths are not discussed in the sources.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Thompson blamed law and custom for women's subordination, but the construction of sex itself is a later debate.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Debates on the category of women are modern and not in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring national martyrs is not discussed in the sources.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Thompson's rationalist utilitarianism treats politics as a matter of happiness and distribution.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora homeland debates are not in the sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cultural nationalism is not discussed in the sources.

god-not-male.rationale: Thompson was an atheist, so the gender of God was not his concern, and the other thinkers are silent.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist scripture criticism is later; Thompson's feminism was not framed through scripture.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative merging by people is not discussed in the sources.

independent-unions.rationale: Hodgskin's defence of combinations and his hostility to a legislature of capitalists imply unions independent of the state.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Bray linked political and economic equality but this is a later Marxist formulation.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Municipal public utilities are not discussed in the sources; Thompson's communities were local but not municipal in this sense.

municipal-property.rationale: Thompson's self-governing communities hold property locally, but others did not propose it.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Thompson's communities were small and self-governing, with some federal links; not detailed.

family-wage.rationale: Hodgskin's claim was for the whole produce of labour, not a family-size wage; Thompson's feminism sits uneasily with a male breadwinner wage.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is anachronistic and not in the sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Life extension research is anachronistic and not in the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Untraceable digital payments are anachronistic, though Gray's labour money is an exchange reform of another sort.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online pseudonymity is anachronistic and not in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Hodgskin's individual natural rights and Thompson's equal-worth ethics favour persons over the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Thompson was an atheist materialist reformer.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Regional autonomy arrangements are not discussed in the sources.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetic engineering is anachronistic and not in the sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban density and environment are anachronistic and not in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from Thompson's universalist equal-worth view.

racial-pride.rationale: Racial pride is not discussed in the sources.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from Thompson's utilitarian peaceful outlook.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred from Thompson's universalist equal-worth utilitarianism; nothing in the school's writings blames social strain on diversity.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed; their concern was class and distribution.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from Hodgskin's free-trade stance; strategic-industry policy is anachronistic.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the Chartist tradition Bray belonged to, which sought a single elected House; not documented for the school.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Never discussed; the school's cooperative communities and class-based analysis of workers versus capitalists point away from ethnolinguistic nationhood, inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Never discussed; Thompson was an atheist egalitarian who wanted equal political rights for all, so religious separate electorates are inferred to be unwelcome.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Never discussed; their grievance was with capitalists and landlords at home, not foreign plots against the country, inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed directly; Thompson's cooperative communities included universal education for all, so free schooling is inferred as mild support.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental externalities were not a concern of the school; Hodgskin's hostility to state action and Thompson's communal planning leave adherents split.

future-generations.rationale: Not discussed; their concern was the distribution of produce between workers and owners, so no stewardship duty is stated.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Thompson argued for women's full equality on utilitarian grounds, not for distinct feminine values, and the other figures were silent.

arms-reduction.rationale: Their remedies were explicitly peaceful and cooperative, so reduced armaments is inferred as mild support, though the topic was not addressed.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; the school's radical, anti-aristocratic stance makes secret dealings between governments an inferred target of mild opposition.

capital-controls.rationale: Gray proposed a national bank and Bray exchange institutions, while Hodgskin favoured free trade and little state action, so adherents split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not addressed; Hodgskin's individualism and Thompson's communities pull in different directions.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the peaceful character of the school's remedies; war resistance is not stated.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Hodgskin defended workers' combinations and the school sought workers' share of produce, but bargaining was secondary to cooperative schemes.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the aim of workers receiving the whole produce through exchange and cooperation, not top-ups from taxation.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; Hodgskin favoured limited government while Gray wanted a national bank, so the four split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed; the school concerned domestic labour and capital rather than international rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The school's remedies were peaceful and varied, so it did not call for destroying the existing state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Remedies ranged from Thompson's cooperative communities to Bray's producers' companies and Hodgskin's free markets, with no single blueprint imposed.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from the school's view of rent as unearned deduction from labour; treating land as valued capital runs against that.

sacred-nation.rationale: Not a theme; the school's focus on class interests and cooperation suggests no sacralised nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; the school's opposition to interest might favour relief, but no view can be sourced.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; the school's exploitation theory was about class and landlords, not regions.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from natural-right claims to the whole produce of labour, notably in Hodgskin; not discussed as human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Anachronistic; Hodgskin would distrust state funding while Thompson might favour public education and information.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Never discussed; Thompson was a secular rationalist, so no single underlying spiritual truth is stated; inferred as neutral.

farm-price-support.rationale: Anachronistic; Gray's national bank and labour money point toward public credit, but Hodgskin opposed state intervention, so adherents split.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic and undiscussed; the school was pacific and anti-war but gave no stance on nuclear weapons; inferred as neutral.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from the claim that workers are entitled to the whole produce; later Owenite and Chartist links suggest working-class organization, but the sources do not discuss parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Thompson's feminism and concern for human welfare, which implies opposing mutilation; adherents did not address it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: William Thompson's Appeal of One Half the Human Race (1825) argued for women's equal legal and property rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Never discussed; no basis in the sources for a position on language classification.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Anachronistic; Hodgskin's individualism supports property-based liability over agency regulation, but the other three favoured collective remedies, so a mild lean.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of hereditary privilege and landlord rents as unearned deductions; chiefs were not addressed.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; the school never addressed environmental limits, and Hodgskin's liberty stress conflicts with state priority; inferred as neutral.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Anachronistic and undiscussed; reformers criticised harsh penal law, but nothing indicates a view on mandatory sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Never discussed; the movement was cosmopolitan in outlook and gave no position on immigration or language.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Thompson and Gray's cooperative schemes and Hodgskin's individualism split on compulsion; the early unions were not discussed in these terms, so adherents are divided.

voter-id.rationale: The school wrote little on electoral administration; inferred as no clear position.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Thompson was a radical secular reformer and Hodgskin a liberal individualist, so neither would give one interpretation legal precedence; inferred from their general liberalism.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Thompson backed radical democracy with social and economic equality, and Hodgskin distrusted political rule; most would want substance beyond elections, but the topic was not addressed in these terms.

premarital-sex.rationale: Thompson, an Owenite, criticised marriage law in Appeal of One Half the Human Race and wanted women's equality; other Ricardians were silent, so this is inferred from Thompson.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the school's hostility to coercive state power, especially Hodgskin's, and from its radical-press tradition of free circulation.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; they aimed to remove unearned deductions from labour through cooperation, labour money and equal exchange rather than a state payment, so a tax-and-transfer fix would be seen as treating symptoms.

women-suffrage.rationale: Thompson's 1825 Appeal of One Half the Human Race argued for equal political and civil rights for women; the other three did not oppose it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Thompson blamed law, custom and men's power over women and was critical of religion, but the school did not make religion the main cause; adherents are not agreed.

race-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; the school did not discuss race, and the concept in its modern form post-dates it.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Thompson wanted women's equality through cooperative communities rather than state offices, and others were silent; inferred as neutral.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Their core claim is that labour, not first occupation, is the title to property, and Thompson and Hodgskin attacked landlords' rent as an unearned deduction; Hodgskin's Lockean strand makes this less than strong.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Never addressed in the 1820s-40s; nothing in the labour theory of value points either way, so no stance is inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: Thompson was a rationalist Owenite and the school's argument rested on political economy, not scripture; the sources do not discuss biblical literalism.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: Thompson wrote the Appeal on behalf of women and wanted equality in cooperative communities, but self-government for Indigenous groups was never discussed.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: their remedies were voluntary cooperation and exchange, not a nationalised planned economy ruled by a bureaucracy; the question is anachronistic.

indirect-election.rationale: Never addressed; Thompson's cooperative communities were democratic but the sources give no view on tiered councils, and Hodgskin opposed state power altogether.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: Thompson and Hodgskin were radical dissenters from the established order and attacked privilege, so a legally privileged church would be unlikely to be favoured.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Never addressed; the school was concerned with class and exchange, not ethnic territory.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Never addressed; no inference from the labour theory of value or cooperative remedies.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic: decolonisation lay a century ahead and the school did not discuss borders.

simple-living.rationale: Adherents sought workers' full produce and abundance through cooperation, not frugality as such, though Thompson's communities stressed modest shared living; they split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: Thompson was an Irish landowner who turned against landlordism and Ascendancy privilege, but the sources do not discuss settlement of indigenous regions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Never addressed; Thompson favoured sexual equality but there is no sourced view on conscription, and Hodgskin opposed state compulsion.

missingStatements.text: Workers are entitled to the whole product of their labour.
missingStatements.rationale: The school's defining claim, that the labourer has a right to the whole produce, which rent, profit and interest unjustly reduce; existing statements capture it only through exploitation and income wording.

missingStatements.text: Goods should be exchanged at prices set by the amount of labour they embody.
missingStatements.rationale: Gray's labour-time currency and Bray's equal exchange priced by labour cost of production make this the school's central practical proposal.
missingStatements.declined: Labour-value pricing is a niche mechanism that would be near-neutral for most ideologies; income-for-work-not-ownership covers the claim.

missingStatements.text: Low wages restrict demand and cause economic gluts and crises.
missingStatements.rationale: The school rejected Say's law and argued that workers' low pay limits demand, an underconsumption theory later used by Marx.

notes: The school was never unified. Hodgskin was an individualist near-anarchist who trusted free markets and opposed state action, Thompson sought voluntary cooperative communities, and Gray and Bray proposed national banking or exchange institutions. Answers on the state, markets and ownership therefore lean neutral or medium. Most answers on modern issues are low-confidence inferences.
